text:
Alexander Wennberg missed 10 games before returning on Nov. 9, and the Sharks put him straight back into the deep end: 23 and 22 minutes in his first two games back, and a spot on the first power-play unit next to Macklin Celebrini, according to Sharks Hockey Digest's Max Miller.

The scoring hasn't followed yet. He has no goals and three assists in 11 games on 2.26 expected goals, after 18 goals and 55 points last season. Our form check calls it mixed: slightly fewer chances than usual (2.1 expected on his own shots over his last ten against 2.5), and the ones he gets aren't going in.

His game was never about finishing. Evolving-Hockey had most of his value last season coming from even-strength defense and drawing penalties, with opponents getting fewer chances while he played (85th percentile). Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking flags a signature: 22% of his setups come from behind the net. Max Miller also noted "a terrific screen in front" on a goal this week. Zero goals is well below what his chances say, and his role looks safe either way.
headline: Alexander Wennberg is back, and so are the minutes
